opening: Old men in these parts say that peace and war are two oxen in one yoke: whichever you drive, the other walks beside it. For five hundred years the house of Sokil held the Hetman's mace, and the land between the Dnipro and the Buh knew a quiet it had never known before. The quiet ended on the day they buried Hetman Sokil the Holy. The mace passed to Oleksandr Verbenko, a decent man who had never wanted to rule. The colonels saw at once that he could not hold them, and each began to carve out a piece of the country for himself while the Hetman drowned his helplessness in wine. The people, who at first had loved him, began to call him Verbenko the Grey. And then, from the west, from the castles of Sandomierz, came Kniaz Dominik Ostrzycki with a cry that the kobzars still sing: "Chyhyryn is dying, and Darkness is rising!" He called it a crusade for order. The Crown gave him banners of hussars, the Khan sent him horsemen, and every landless sabre on the road fell in behind him. So began the years the chronicles call the Dark Years.

The colonels who had been quietly robbing the Hetman were not about to let a Polish kniaz rob him first. Each gathered his regiment, called it the defence of the mace, and marched on Chyhyryn. Within a year every road to the capital was full of armies, and nobody could say any longer who was fighting for whom. What was left of the Hetman's authority blew away like chaff. In that storm, between the great names, walked thousands of men nobody wrote down: hired sabres who sold a day of their life for a handful of silver. This is the story of one of them.
So you have found your way to the Motronyn Monastery.
I will not ask what brought you here, and you will not tell me. The brotherhood keeps one rule, and whoever wants to walk out of these gates alive keeps it too: you win. Nothing else is asked of you.

Lose a fight, and you will be left on the field for the crows, but it is the brotherhood that pays the greater price for your failure. If you are cut in battle, hold on. Our brothers know how to close a wound before you have time to notice it.
Pick your work with your head, not your heart. How you win is your own business, so long as you win. A victory is yours alone. A defeat belongs to all of us.
The Dark Years have turned the whole country upside down. No one knows how it will end, but every sabre you take tilts the scales a little. Do not take them lightly.
We will speak again. Remember the one rule. Live through this miserable age, and perhaps you will help build the next one. God keep you, warrior.

talk: 0|[Messenger] Sir, everyone knows that this peace was bought with your sabre as much as anyone's. The Hetman wishes to thank you. He offers you a sotnia in his own army and a house in Chyhyryn. Will you take it?
No. I was born with a sabre in my fist, and the steppe raised me. I would rot behind city walls... and there are fights still waiting for me.
It is a great honour. I will try to be worthy of it.
0|[Messenger] A wise choice. The Hetman will be glad to hear it.
pictures: 2|But fate does not let a man like me sit by the stove. Not one of the colonels of the Steppe cares about the people who feed them. They want the mace, not peace. Villages burn, and the dead do not ask who was right. I have too much on my conscience to rest now.

3|Eighty-two years after the start of the Dark Years, Hetman Zinovii Zhuravel, whose father had once ridden under Colonel Chornohuz, took the mace in a lawful election from Hetman Tryhub, the son of Hetmanka Olena. He was a just man and a hard one, and he gathered the whole country under one banner for the first time since Sokil the Holy. From that day the land was known as the Grand Duchy of Ruthenia.
4|I gave the sotnia back to the Hetman and returned to the Motronyn Monastery. All my life I had dreamed of a time when heroes would be needed again. The dream was not done with me yet.

Looking for me? Who are you?

She did. What of it?
37|[Marusia] She always said that the man she gave that scarf to would be the one to take me from our house.
That is a child's tale.
37|[Marusia] Then let it be a tale. I am still coming with you.
I cannot. I am a hired sabre. I have no house and no tomorrow.
37|[Marusia] Oksana trusted you with the last thing she had. That is enough for me.
This is madness... and yet I believe you. Very well. Come. We are leaving this place.
37|[Marusia] Yes...
pictures: 7|It was the hardest choice of my life, and I made it: I took Marusia with me and we were married before the first snow. I swore to her that I was done with the monastery and the brotherhood, and that I would plough a field like other men. On the road home I felt something I had never felt before. It took me a long time to understand that it was peace.

talk: I need to be back before dark.

The Seal? I have no idea what you mean.
0|[Colonel Topolia] Do not play the fool with me. Shoot him!
A poisoned arrow...!
0|[Colonel Topolia] Go and meet your Maker, you greedy cur. Now then... yes! Here it is, the Seal!
I do not die that easily... And whose hands are bloodier, colonel, mine or yours?
0|[Colonel Topolia] Impossible... the poison should have... no!

0|[Colonel Topolia] ARRR!

pictures: 8|So ends a hired sabre who served no one, loved no one and died in a ditch chasing a nobleman's gold. There is no name on his cross.

talk: 34|[Colonel Chornohuz] Strange... one small thing overlooked, and it cost me everything.
May God give your soul rest.
pictures: 9|He had despised his enemy, and for that a hero lay dead on the field.
8|It does not matter how strong a man is or how many sabres ride behind him. No one outruns his fate. Every old soldier knows that fate is the one enemy that has never lost a battle.

talk: 4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] You? Standing in front of me? Do you know who I am, boy? There is not a man between the Dnipro and the Vistula who does not fear my name. I am ZADERYKHVIST!
4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] Still on your feet. Well, well. I will say it plainly: you have done fine work out there.
My thanks.
4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] Why not ride under my banner?
I am sorry. I cannot.
4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] I thought you would say that. Such a waste...
4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] A man like you cannot be left alive to sell himself to my enemies tomorrow.
You would...!
4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] Die well, mercenary!
Not today!
4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] ARRR!
Now you know, Butcher. You bleed like the rest of the meat you chopped.
4|[Colonel Zaderykhvist] ...Ugh... impossible... how...?!
Sleep. For good.
pictures: 8|When the Butcher fell, the terror that had held his regiment together fell with him. His men scattered in a single night and left his body to the ravens.
10|He died on my sabre, and I have never once regretted it. That evening I drank a cup of good wine to a land with one murderer fewer in it.

talk: 0|[Colonel Kharko] At last! The whole north-east is mine!
Well fought, colonel.
0|[Colonel Kharko] I owe you more than I can say.
You flatter me.
0|[Colonel Kharko] I will pay you as a colonel pays, not as a merchant does.
I am obliged.
0|[Colonel Kharko] Ha! Now Kharko has wings, and the whole Hetmanate will see him fly!
33|[Colonel Bairak] ...
pictures: 1|By breaking Colonel Tuman, Kharko became a man to be reckoned with overnight, and every tavern in the Hetmanate talked of his rise.
11|But his men never truly believed in him. He lacked the iron to stand up to his own osauls, and the best of them left him one by one.
8|In the end Chornohuz's regiment broke what was left of Kharko's army, and he lost every acre he had won. Kharko had wanted to fly, and he had not had the wisdom to be content with walking.

11|[Tymish] I am asking you, sir.
pictures: 12|Tymish talked me into it, and I took up what Kosach had left behind. I was a plain soldier, and now a regiment looked to me for orders. A whole new life was beginning, whether I wanted it or not.

I must be going.

My thanks, colonel, but I ride alone. At least for now.
0|[Colonel Shulha] A pity.
Farewell, colonel.
0|[Colonel Shulha] Should you think better of it, you know where to find me.

8|Colonel Shulha, who had barely crawled off the field when his regiment broke, slid downhill from that day on. He died alone, poor and unmourned.
6|Where is the colonel I was born to serve?

If only I had been stronger!

What will you do now?

And if you cannot?
1|[Osaul Zalizo] Then I will keep looking until I can.
1|[Osaul Zalizo] Thank you for everything.
1|[Osaul Zalizo] Until we meet again.
pictures: 13|Zalizo slipped through Chornohuz's lines and was gone from the Hetmanate. I envied Colonel Bairak that day. Few men ever earn such loyalty from a man so honest and so hard.

0|[Colonel Tuman] And you, friend. You did more than any three of my osauls today.
0|[Colonel Tuman] Those eyes of yours... a wolf's eyes. I like that.
0|[Colonel Tuman] Serve me, and you will never regret it.
pictures: 3|After that battle Tuman was the strongest man in the Hetmanate, and for a short while his regiments held Chyhyryn itself.

8|But Chornohuz was not done. He raised a new army, bought the newest guns money could find, and crushed Tuman so completely that the colonel had to flee Chyhyryn in a woman's dress. He reached his home alive, but the whole Hetmanate had seen him run, and he never lived it down.
14|The shame curdled into hatred, and he died a bitter, lonely old man. Fate, as always, had the last word over the plans of men.

After the long war he had himself proclaimed Hetman all the same, and no ruler before him had held so much. What Bairak and all his allies could not do, a fever did: he sickened in camp and died before his rule reached the far edges of the land. Twenty-two years after Chornohuz's death...

34|[Colonel Chornohuz] At last! At last I have you!

33|[Colonel Bairak] Do you not see it, Chornohuz? All of this is for nothing. We will only bury more of the innocent.

34|[Colonel Chornohuz] Take his head, and bury him with the honours of a hero!

pictures: 5|And so, in a single morning, one of the finest men of the Hetmanate was gone. Colonel Bairak, kin to the Hetman and the only colonel who had fought for Verbenko's house to the end, passed into the chronicles.
12|His osauls Hrebinka and Zalizo followed him into the grave before the year was out.
4|Every spring, even now, people who remember Bairak and his two osauls bring cherry blossom to their graves. They say the scent of it can teach loyalty even to a hired sabre.

Your greed did this, not I.
34|[Colonel Chornohuz] You dare speak to me so?!
34|[Colonel Chornohuz] Kill me, and my heirs will hunt you down. My name will not die with me!
1|[Osaul Zalizo] Let him go.

You would break the law of the sabre?
1|[Osaul Zalizo] The law of the sabre is worth nothing to a man with a stone on his soul. I keep my own law too.

34|[Colonel Chornohuz] Ha! My thanks, Zalizo! Consider the debt paid in full!
1|[Osaul Zalizo] Ride, while I still let you. And do not cross my path again!
pictures: 8|Zalizo's sense of honour did him credit, and it let one of the worst murderers of the age walk away. The fates do not like to be cheated. Zalizo himself died badly on a battlefield not many years later.
14|Had Chornohuz died in that fight, the whole history of the land would have run another way. But the future belongs to fate alone.

pictures: 13|Topolia turned out to be a fair master, but what he built did not outlive him. His will left his lands to Colonel Bairak, and nobody honoured it. His family fought over the estate until the whole of it fell into the hands of Colonel Sych.

15|Sych wanted no one left to challenge his claim, so he had every last Topolia murdered. A whole house wiped out between one harvest and the next. The colonel had believed in honour. His children had believed in gold, and it buried them.

talk: 33|[Colonel Bairak] Damn it! I took them too lightly.

pictures: 3|On Osaul Ternovyi's advice, Bairak threw his whole regiment into Podillia. He fought like a man with nothing left to lose, and Podillia fell to him. He held it fast and added it to lands that were already wide.
1|Ternovyi, who had drawn up the plan for Podillia, was called the Magnificent from that campaign on.
9|The old saying is true: strength is given to the stubborn man who will not yield. Had Bairak given up Podillia and ridden home, the Hetmanate would surely have slid into the abyss.

1|[Osaul Zalizo] Soon!

10|[Shram] A rare man, that one. Eh?
18|[Nazar] Aye. I would gladly share a jug with him some day.
I must go.
10|[Shram] Go, then. God speed you, warrior.
pictures: 10|Colonel Hulak lost his lands in the end, not to an enemy but to a plot hatched in his own house, and his two best osauls could do nothing to stop it. The blow caught him with his guard down: he had felt safe with his own men around him. Plainly it had always been written that Shram and Nazar would end up riding for Bairak.

14|Shram became one of the finest commanders Podillia ever had. Among his deeds was the destruction of Rotmistr Zaremba's banner to the last man. Nazar, too, became Podillia's man in time; his great work was the bridgehead that joined Podillia to the heart of the Hetmanate.

33|[Colonel Bairak] ...
35|[Colonel Bilous] Why did you come at me with a sabre?
33|[Colonel Bairak] ...

33|[Colonel Bairak] ...
35|[Colonel Bilous] It was yours for the asking...
33|[Colonel Bairak] ...! What?!
35|[Colonel Bilous] Go.
33|[Colonel Bairak] ...! What kind of man are you...
pictures: 14|Bilous had grown fat on other men's land during the war, and it was Bairak's coming that put an end to his grabbing.

15|Bilous let Bairak go, and Bairak went on to take Podillia by Ternovyi's plan. When he met Bilous again, he needed no plan at all: someone inside Bilous's own camp had sold him out. They caught his men in a trap, and one more hero passed into the songs of the kobzars.

34|[Colonel Chornohuz] I will be back!

34|[Colonel Chornohuz] Nothing against you personally. You are simply standing in my road.
36|[Colonel Rudyi] Is that so?
34|[Colonel Chornohuz] Yes. In my road to Bairak. I will have his head, and I will have it!
36|[Colonel Rudyi] I see. So this is about more than a few acres...
34|[Colonel Chornohuz] A real man burns to be the greatest. Anything less is not worth living for.

pictures: 1|Rudyi ruled well and ruled honestly. He let the church guide his people and made plain dealing the law of his estate. His land was small, but it lay where the roads from Podillia into the heart of the country met.

3|Before long Chornohuz's attacks wore him down, and he fled his land with the shirt on his back and nothing more. Yet Chornohuz respected the man's convictions. He revoked the death sentence he had passed and let Rudyi return to his own house.
6|Rudyi was one of the unluckiest men in the land. In a quieter age he would have been a truly great master.

You owe me nothing.

Of course. Send for me when you need me.

13|Kurylo had built his regiment in the shadow of his father's terrible death, and with Rudyi's help he meant to build a better army than any before. He never had the time. Two years after taking Podillia, Hlib Kurylo died, only forty-eight years old.
3|Even Kurylo, one of the greatest soldiers the Hetmanate ever raised, could not step out of the long shadow of his fate.

Think nothing of it.

I have to say it: I have never seen loyalty like yours.

pictures: 12|The Zalizo whose name was dragged through the mud after Sych's attack was not the Zalizo I knew. As Bairak's loyal osaul he had beaten Oksana at Chortomlyk and cut down Pereima and Brzeski, two of the best sabres in the Hetmanate. But he quarrelled too often with Ternovyi, and so he was sent to the front line against Sych, where he was left alone, cut off from his own people. His journey back to Bairak became a legend of its own, though the fire in him had burned low by the time he grew old.

1|Zalizo named me his successor, and I became the first commander of Podillia. He also handed me his title of Knight of the Hetman's Banner, and then he left the wars for good. From that day they called me the Banner Knight, and my life as a hero began.

gamestr: That was how I walked away from the fields of slaughter. They gave me a sotnia and a roof, and I no longer had to roam from one battle to the next.
[Messenger] The country still needs men like you.
